# openobserve_downtime (Resource)

Manages an OpenObserve downtime: a maintenance window during which alerts, anomaly detections and synthetics checks are muted, and SLOs are corrected.

**Requires OpenObserve Enterprise v1.2.0-rc1 or later.** An open-source or older server is refused with a diagnostic saying so.

A downtime is one-time (`schedule.repeat = "none"`, from `starts_at` to `ends_at`) or recurring (`daily` or `weekly`, a window of `duration_secs` starting at `start_time_local` in `timezone`). Each `target` block picks a module and narrows it by folder, ID or (for synthetics) tag, and `condition` narrows every module but synthetics by the dimensions of what fires.

The server keeps a downtime after it ends, for history, and an ended one-time downtime stays in state with `status = "ended"`. A downtime cancelled in the UI also stays, with `status = "cancelled"` or `"ended_early"`, and is not scheduled again by an update: replace it (for example with `terraform apply -replace`) to schedule it anew. The server deletes ended and cancelled downtimes after its retention period (`O2_DOWNTIMES_RETENTION_DAYS`, 90 days or more). One that was ended or cancelled when it was last read then stays in state as it was, rather than being created again, so a cancelled window does not come back.

Destroying a downtime that is active or scheduled cancels it first, which the server requires, then deletes it. A downtime that already corrected SLO slices cannot be deleted at all: it is cancelled, removed from state with a warning, and removed by the server's retention once the SLO window has passed.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Downtimes need OpenObserve Enterprise v1.2.0-rc1 or later.

# A one-time maintenance window: mute the checkout alerts during a database
# upgrade, and tell the on-call channel when it starts and ends.
resource "openobserve_downtime" "db_upgrade" {
  name        = "Checkout DB upgrade"
  reason      = "Postgres 16 upgrade, CHG-1234"
  show_banner = true

  # Only what fires for the checkout service.
  condition = jsonencode({
    type     = "pair"
    key      = "service"
    operator = "="
    value    = "checkout"
  })

  target {
    module = "alerts"
  }
  target {
    module = "anomaly_detections"
  }

  schedule {
    starts_at = "2026-12-05T22:00:00Z"
    ends_at   = "2026-12-06T01:00:00Z"
  }

  notifications {
    destinations = [openobserve_alert_destination.oncall.name]
    events       = ["started", "ending_soon", "ended"]
  }
}

# A recurring window: every Saturday and Sunday from 02:00 to 03:00 Berlin
# time, mute the synthetics checks tagged `batch`, and count the SLO's
# minutes in that window as good.
resource "openobserve_downtime" "weekend_batch" {
  name        = "Weekend batch jobs"
  show_banner = false

  target {
    module = "synthetics"
    tags   = ["batch"]
  }
  target {
    module   = "slos"
    ids      = [openobserve_slo.checkout_availability.slo_id]
    slo_mode = "count_as_good"
  }

  schedule {
    repeat           = "weekly"
    weekdays         = [6, 7]
    starts_at        = "2026-12-01T00:00:00Z"
    timezone         = "Europe/Berlin"
    start_time_local = "02:00"
    duration_secs    = 3600
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name shown in the downtime list and on the banner, at most 256 characters, with no leading or trailing spaces.

### Optional

- `condition` (String) Dimension condition, as a JSON document; build it with `jsonencode()`. It narrows every target whose module has dimensions (all but synthetics) to the items it matches. A pair is `{type = "pair", key = "service", operator = "=", value = "checkout"}`, with `operator` `=` or `!=`, and a `value` that may end in `*` to match a prefix. A group is `{type = "group", op = "and", items = [...]}`, with `op` `and` or `or`.

Keys must be written exactly, with no surrounding spaces. The server lowercases values, so `Checkout` matches `checkout`, and every way to satisfy the condition must include an `=` pair: `!=` alone cannot silence everything. Keys are the semantic dimensions of the organization (such as `service` or `env`); the server refuses a key it does not know.
- `folder_id` (String) Downtime folder that holds the downtime, from an `openobserve_folder` with `folder_type = "downtimes"`. Defaults to `default`. Changing it moves the downtime in place.
- `notifications` (Block, Optional) Announce the downtime's events to alert destinations. Omit it to announce nothing. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--notifications))
- `org_id` (String) Organization identifier. Defaults to the provider's `org_id`.
- `reason` (String) Why the downtime exists, at most 1000 characters.
- `schedule` (Block, Optional) When the downtime applies. Required. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--schedule))
- `show_banner` (Boolean) Show a warning banner to everyone in the organization while a window is active. Defaults to `true`.
- `target` (Block List) A module the downtime covers, at most one block per module. At least one is required. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--target))

### Read-Only

- `downtime_id` (String) Server-assigned downtime ID.
- `id` (String) Resource ID in the format `{org_id}/{downtime_id}`.
- `status` (String) Where the downtime is now: `scheduled`, `active`, `ended`, `cancelled`, or `ended_early` (cancelled during a window). Read when the resource is refreshed.

<a id="nestedblock--notifications"></a>
### Nested Schema for `notifications`

Optional:

- `destinations` (Set of String) Names of `openobserve_alert_destination` resources to notify, 1 to 10. Required in the block.
- `ending_soon_lead_secs` (Number) How long before the end the `ending_soon` event is sent, in seconds. Defaults to 600. With `ending_soon`, it must be at least 60 and no longer than the window.
- `events` (Set of String) Events to announce: `started`, `ending_soon`, `ended`, `cancelled` and `extended`. At least one is required in the block.


<a id="nestedblock--schedule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `schedule`

Optional:

- `duration_secs` (Number) Recurring downtimes only: how long each window lasts, from 60 seconds to 7 days, and no longer than the time between repeats. Required for `daily` and `weekly`. A one-time downtime reports its span here.
- `ends_at` (String) End, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. Required for a one-time downtime, whose window runs from `starts_at` to `ends_at`, at least a minute and at most 7 days. For a recurring downtime it is optional, and only its date in `timezone` counts: the last day the schedule applies, inclusive.
- `repeat` (String) `none` (one-time, the default), `daily` or `weekly`.
- `start_time_local` (String) Recurring downtimes only: when each window starts, as `HH:MM` in `timezone`. Required for `daily` and `weekly`.
- `starts_at` (String) Start, as an RFC 3339 timestamp such as `2026-12-01T22:00:00Z`. For a recurring downtime it is the first day the schedule applies from. Required.
- `timezone` (String) IANA timezone of `start_time_local` and of a recurring downtime's days, such as `Europe/Berlin`. Defaults to `UTC`.
- `weekdays` (Set of Number) Weekly downtimes only: the days a window starts, 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday).


<a id="nestedblock--target"></a>
### Nested Schema for `target`

Required:

- `module` (String) `alerts`, `anomaly_detections`, `synthetics` or `slos`.

Optional:

- `folder_ids` (Set of String) Folders of the module to cover, at most 50. Omit it to cover every folder.
- `ids` (Set of String) IDs of the items to cover, at most 200: alert IDs, anomaly detection IDs, synthetics check IDs or SLO IDs. Omit it to cover every item the other settings select.
- `incident_mode` (String) Alerts only: what a muted firing does to incidents. `muted`, the default, records the incident as muted; `none` opens no incident at all.
- `slo_mode` (String) SLOs only: how the window counts toward the SLO. `exclude` leaves its minutes out, `count_as_good` counts them as good. The server's default is `exclude`.
- `tags` (Set of String) Synthetics only: tags of the checks to cover, at most 16, in lowercase.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Downtimes are imported as {org_id}/{downtime_id}, or as a bare
# {downtime_id} in the provider's organization. The downtime_id is in the
# downtime's URL in the UI, or in GET /api/v2/{org_id}/downtimes.
terraform import openobserve_downtime.db_upgrade default/3LidhdqdOAv068f3A3B8XUOAX9w
```
